english.html: [was wont to] say and do before going away [unclear: the French has no verb between Martin and dire].

He could not have addressed himself better, inasmuch as friends, kinsfolk, household servants and neighbours are those who commonly know and understand the acts of the persons to whom they belong by right of kinship, friendship, familiarity or neighbourhood. Kinsfolk (say our Jurisconsults) have knowledge, in all likelihood, of what their kinsfolk do, of their estate, condition and quality <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>; and so likewise do neighbours among themselves <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>: so that he who says he does not know the estate or the deeds of his kinsman or neighbour cannot be excused under the pretext of the ignorance that he alleges <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>. Which must be understood to be true of things which in all likelihood fall within the knowledge of a kinsman or a neighbour: such as the health or the age of a kinsman <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>, the poverty or wealth <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>, dwelling <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>, marriage <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>, reputation and renown <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup> of a neighbour; and generally all acts which cannot be done, dispatched or properly carried through save by the succession of time, requiring some length and interval <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>. For the things which are done among kinsfolk or in the neighbourhood, and can be brought very soon to an end and completed in a little time, do not easily pass into the knowledge of the other kinsfolk and neighbours, because they are most often done secretly — as a contract, a will, a crime <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>. For even what is done in public once only is not to be presumed to be known by all persons, seeing that such an act has had no duration <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>; although it is commonly said that of what is done in public no one may allege or pretend ignorance <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>.

Il ne ſe pouuoit mieux adreſſer, d'autãt que les amis,
parens, domeſtiques, & voiſins ſont ceux-là qui com-
munemẽt, ſçauent, & entendent les actes des perſonnes,
auſquelles ils appartiennent par droit de parenté, ami-
tié, familiarité ou voiſinage. Les parens (diſent nos Iu-
riſconſultes) ont cognoiſſance vraye, ſemblablement
de ce que leurs parens font, de leur eſtat, condition, &
qualité {a}. & de meſme les voiſins entr'eux {b}. de manie-
re que celuy qui dit ne ſçauoir point l'eſtat, ou les faits
de ſon parent, ou voiſin, ne peut eſtre excuſé ſous pre-
texte de l'ignorance, qu'il allegue {c}. Ce qu'il faut enten-
dre eſtre veritable és choſes, qui tombent vray ſembla-
blement en la cognoiſſance d'vn parent, ou d'vn voi-
ſin: comme la ſanté, ou l'aage d'vn parent {d}, la pauure-
té, ou richeſſe {e}, habitation {f}, le mariage {g}, la reputa-
tion, & renommée {h} du voiſin: & generalement tous
actes, qui ne ſe peuuent faire deſpeſcher, ou expliquer
proprement: mais par la ſucceſſion de temps, deſirans
quelque longueur, & interualle {i}. Car les choſes qui ſe
font entre les parens, ou au voiſinage, & peuuent eſtre
menées bien toſt à fin, & paracheuees en peu de temps,
ne paſſent pas facilement en la cognoiſſance des au-
tres parens & voiſins, par ce qu'elles ſont le plus ſouuẽt
faites ſecrettement. Comme vn contract, vn teſtament,
vn crime {k}. Car meſmes ce qu'eſt faict en public vne
fois ſeulement, n'eſt à preſumer eſtre ſceu de toutes per
ſonnes: veu que tel acte n'a point eu de durée {l}. Bien
qu'on dit communemẽt, que de ce qu'eſt fait en public
nul puiſſe alleguer, ou pretendre ignorance {m}.
